Wow!  Sorry for the short notice on this one (applications due tonight).

*Fellowship Applications Due Tonight!*
Applications for SAGA’s flagship program, <https://saga.stanford.edu/fellowships|the Fall 2026 AI Safety Fellowship>, are *due tonight at 11:59 PM*!
*<https://airtable.com/appmbyqTx5igfU6eZ/paghS181zeEshjLXN/form|Apply>*

From <@U0ALWMKR3CZ> :
>  :mega: *DISPATCH: AI Safety Comms Fellowship · applications close Oct 10*
> 
> AI safety has a communications bottleneck. When an AI incident breaks, the story that gets traction shapes what the public and legislators believe. The field doesn't have enough people who can explain the incident quickly and make it go viral.
> 
> DISPATCH is a 6-week, fully remote fellowship (~15 hrs/week) to change that. Fellows ship 3–4 short-form videos a week and get rapidly upskilled by AI safety professionals and social media pros.
> 
> *What you get*
> • Weekly workshops on specific short-form skills
> • Mentor feedback on your videos every week
> • A portfolio of published AI safety content
> • Support getting placed into AI safety comms roles afterward
> 
> *Who we're looking for*
> Strong AI safety context is a must: you should be able to explain the core arguments for AI risk accurately and on the fly. On top of that, we're especially excited about people who:
> • have made viral shorts/reels (on any topic)
> • can write really good Twitter threads
> • do animation, editing or podcast clipping (big plus if you use Claude to speed it up)
> • are comfortable on camera and good at explaining technical ideas
> 
> Open to applicants anywhere.
> 
> > "I think communications to the public about AI safety is probably the most neglected and important area of work for mitigating risks from AI at the moment." — Agus Covarrubias, co-founder of Kairos
> 
> :point_right: *Apply by Oct 10*: <https://aiscommsfellowship.vercel.app>
> :raising_hand: Know someone who'd be great? Nominate them on the site.

A BBC journalist is working on a documentary showing the pitfalls of AI and would like to talk to red teamers who could jailbreak frontier AI models. Please let me know if you are interested and I am happy to put you in touch with him.

Wednesday is really hump day job-wise :slightly_smiling_face: (80K hours posts)
> • Tarbell Center for AI Journalism: *<https://jobs.80000hours.org/?jobPk=21159&utm_source=job-board-slack-alerts|Tarbell Fellowship>*
> 
> • Encode: *<https://jobs.80000hours.org/?jobPk=21160&utm_source=job-board-slack-alerts|Chief of Staff>*

It's a great day!  David Krueger’s Evitable is hiring communications and community roles in the bay area!
> 
> Director of Community Organizing
> This senior role leads Evitable's movement program, from recruiting volunteer leaders to running public campaigns.
> Location: San Francisco Bay Area (in-person)
> Salary: $140,000 to $175,000 + benefits
> Priority deadline: October 30, 2026
> Job description: <https://evitable.com/dir-community-organizing|evitable.com/dir-community-organizing>
> 
> Communications Manager
> This role owns Evitable's day-to-day content, including social media and the monthly newsletter.
> Location: San Francisco Bay Area (in-person)
> Salary: $85,000 to $130,000 + benefits
> Deadline: October 26, 2026
> Job description: <https://evitable.com/communications-manager|evitable.com/communications-manager>
> 
> Both roles would suit candidates who understand AI risk and want to help bring the conversation to the public.

And!!!

> :mega: *Tarbell Fellowship applications are open!*
> 
> This is a paid fellowship for journalists who want to cover AI, or for AI folks who want to become journalists.
> 
> What you’ll get:
> • 3 months of AI journalism training, then a 9-month newsroom placement
> • All expenses paid weeklong in-person summit
> • Stipend of $75k-$120k (up to $135k for senior fellows with 7+ years’ experience)
> 
> Past fellows have gone to Bloomberg, The Guardian, NBC, TIME and more.
> 
> :date: June 2027 – May 2028
> :alarm_clock: Apply by Nov. 22: <https://airtable.com/appT0usUxWCyFtqOE/pag5NuccaHiv8yPSg/form|airtable.com/appT0usUxWCyFtqOE/…/form>
> :globe_with_meridians: For more details, visit our website: <https://www.tarbellcenter.org/fellowship|tarbellcenter.org/fellowship>
> 
> Please share with anyone who’d be a great fit! :raised_hands:

> :earth_africa: *Apply for GCP's AI Safety Workshop for working professionals in London (6-9th of November)*
> 
> The last few weeks have brought AI safety into the mainstream. Dario Amodei called on the industry to <https://www.pacingthefrontier.com/|pace the frontier>, OpenAI disclosed that its own agents had autonomously broken into <https://metr.org/blog/2026-08-26-openai-hugging-face-incident-investigation/#~1200-agents-sent-%3E70,000-messages-and-files-on-an-unsanctioned-message-board,-and-~700-attacked-hugging-face|Hugging Face> and the <https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c6vgy0333dppo|Australian government,> and Jacob Coxon's <https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/anthropic-researcher-quits-over-out-of-control-ai-fears-707b7628|resignation from Anthropic> was noticed by millions around the globe. If you have been following this and wondering where someone with your background and skills fits in, this workshop is for you.
> We are bringing around 30 mid-career and senior professionals to London for three days to speak to some of the brightest minds in AI safety and help you work out how to move into AI safety.
> 
> This workshop follows <https://www.lateralworkshop.org/|Lateral>, the workshop we ran in Berkeley earlier this month, where attendees spent the weekend with guests from the AI Futures Project, MATS, Constellation, MIRI, METR, Redwood, the UK AI Security Institute and 80,000 Hours. Events like these have played a outsized role in accelerating many of the people now doing the most important work in the field.
> 
> *What you'll do*
> • Speak directly with leading researchers, policy people, operators, and fieldbuilders about how they read the current moment
> • Think through what a move into AI safety looks like for someone with your background, and where you can best deploy your skills
> • Build relationships with other professionals considering similar career transitions
> *Logistics*
> • :spiral_calendar_pad: The workshop takes place Friday, the 6th of November to Monday morning, the 9th of November in London
> • :white_check_mark: Travel, accommodation and meals covered
> • :dart: Best fit: you have some AI safety context already and are thinking seriously about working on it
> • :mortar_board: For students and recent graduates: separate workshops start from January 2027, express interest <https://airtable.com/appX8Lk5WVcPuX4rj/pagRiAko07bIete6c/form|here>
> :alarm_clock: *Applications close Friday, the 9th of October (Anywhere on Earth). Learn more and apply <https://gcp-apply.kairos-project.org/?utm_source=mats&utm_medium=slack&utm_campaign=gcp-london-26|here>!*
